advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the short-circuit tests distinguish the guarded path: build a real tracker (tmp dir) whose graph WOULD register a cycle for a blocking relation, then assert a non-blocking relation returns False on that same graph (so removing the short-circuit flips the result).
evidence: tests/unit/test_blocking_relation_partition.py:66: `_graph.check_would_create_cycle("a", "b", relation, "/nonexistent-tracker") is False`
tests/unit/test_blocking_relation_partition.py:73: `assert _graph.check_would_create_cycle("a", "b", "endorses", "/nonexistent-tracker") is False`
src/rebar/graph/_graph.py:212-226: after the short-circuit, both branches compute `_get_all_blocked_by(...)` and test membership; with an empty graph the membership is `False`.

src/rebar/graph/_graph.py:169-186 + 144-149: `_get_all_blocked_by` walks via `bfs`; `_dependents_of` catches OSError from `os.listdir` on a nonexistent dir and returns nothing, and `os.path.isdir` is False, so the accumulator is empty → `target_id in set()` is `False` regardless of the relation.

ABSENCE: no test drives a REAL backing graph where a hypothetical non-blocking relation, if it fell through to the `else`, would be cycle-checked and wrongly rejected — i.e. the observable contract stated in the module docstring ('a valid link is REJECTED with CyclicDependencyError') is never exercised.
advisory.finding: The two AC2 tests (`test_a_non_blocking_relation_is_never_cycle_checked`, `test_a_hypothetical_new_non_blocking_relation_short_circuits`) are regression-blind: they call `check_would_create_cycle(..., "/nonexistent-tracker")` and assert `is False`, but with a nonexistent tracker dir `_get_all_blocked_by` returns an empty set, so the function returns `False` for ANY relation even if the `if relation not in _BLOCKING_RELATIONS: return False` short-circuit were deleted. Inverting the guard does not make these tests fail, so they cannot catch the regression the diff protects against.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct a tmp tracker where source and target participate in a real blocks/depends_on chain (so `check_would_create_cycle(source, target, 'depends_on', dir)` is True), then assert that the SAME endpoints with a non-blocking relation return False — a change that makes the assertion sensitive to the short-circuit rather than to an empty graph.
